messages:
Alex: quick sync — want to land a safe per-layer partial-quant rollout plan. goal: 1.6-2x token cost reduction without violating p95 latency SLO (<=40ms) or quality regression >1.5% on our eval set.
Mira: +1. rough idea: exclude embeddings & lm_head, calibrate sensitive layers, use int8 for feedforwards, fp8 for attention if stable.
Raj: can we get a short profiler pass first? need layer-wise timings + KV cache delta (warm vs steady). I suspect kv cache warmup is the regressor.
Sam: noted. I'll run three benches: (A) baseline fp16, (B) full-int8, (C) per-layer partial with embedding/lm_head excluded. small and medium seq lengths: 32/128, batch sizes 1/4.
Alex: thanks. config snippet for (C) — keep it consistent with runtime flags:
```
--model rw-13B
--quantization mode=partial
--exclude_layers embed,lm_head
--quant_layers ranges=[0:10, -6:-1]
--kernel_pref int8_gemm_v2,fp8_attn
--batching dynamic,max_batch=8,max_tokens=2048
```
Mira: for calibration use 1280 random tokens from our calibration corpus (mix of open-domain + product prompts). use per-layer KL and cosine of activations to detect shift.
Raj: CI Bot — please kick a profiling job for fp16 & partial-quant for seq128,b1 and seq32,b4, with KV warm and steady traces. tag with `per-layer-quant-probe-1893`.
CI Bot: started perf job per-layer-quant-probe-1893. queued on perf-runner-3. estimate ~22m.
Lina: quick ask — surface per-layer quality delta in Console under Optimize -> regressions. Put the layer index + delta % and example prompts.
Cheng: FYI, earlier we saw weird perf when attention used fp8 kernels on older GPUs (driver issue). add device tag in job metadata.
CI Bot: perf job finished: summary attached.
CI Bot: results (excerpt):
```
Test A: fp16, seq128 b1 (steady): p95=28.4ms, throughput=110 tokens/s, cost_unit=1.00
Test B: full-int8, seq128 b1 (steady): p95=36.1ms, throughput=160 tokens/s, cost_unit=0.58, quality_delta=+3.2% (bad)
Test C: partial-quant (exclude embed/lm_head, layers [0:11,-4:-1]), seq128 b1 (steady): p95=32.2ms, throughput=145 tokens/s, cost_unit=0.65, quality_delta=+0.9%
KV warm traces: first 20 tokens (cold): latency spike +45% on all quant configs; steady-state after 64 tokens.
Seq32 b4: partial-quant p95=18.7ms (vs fp16 16.2ms)
```
Mira: interesting — partial quant gives decent cost savings and quality within tolerance, but p95 for b1/seq128 is 32.2ms which is still under 40ms SLO. need to understand warm spikes from KV warm.
Raj: suspect two contributors: (1) kernel selection fallback for some layers causing extra memcpy/format conversion, (2) cache population overhead for quantized KV layout.
Sam: I profiled single-request timeline: found multiple kernel switches around layer 10 where we fallback from int8_gemm_v2 -> fp32_gemm due to per-layer scale mismatch. that causes ~3.8ms stall per switch.
Alex: actionable: (A) tighten kernel selector so fallback happens earlier at compile time instead of per-invocation, (B) add KV layout write-through warmup to amortize first-request cost, (C) tune dynamic batching default for small-batch low-latency flows.
Mira: on calibration: if we calibrate with shorter sequences we may under-estimate activation ranges for deep layers — leads to overflow/fallback. use mixed-length calibration (16/64/256 samples).
Lina: for Console, we should add a per-route metric: "layer_fallback_count" and surface top-3 fallback layers per model. Ops can then map to model config.
Cheng: for kernel selector heuristics — proposal: precompute a layer-level profile during model onboarding and store a kernel hint table keyed by model_version + device + seq_length_bucket. runtime consults hint, attempts kernel, and only falls back if hardware error.
Raj: agree. storing hint table also helps Dedicated customers where devices are fixed. fallback penalties are much more predictable then.
Sam: experiment request: run the partial-quant job again with explicit kernel hints forcing int8_gemm_v2 on all FF layers and measure fallback_count + p95. I can push flag `--kernel_hint_force=true` to perf runner.
CI Bot: scheduled job per-layer-quant-probe-1893-hint for device perf-runner-3.
CI Bot: job done. summary:
```
Partial-quant + kernel_hints, seq128 b1: p95=30.0ms, fallback_count=2 (layers 10, 32), throughput=152 tok/s, quality_delta=+0.95%
Partial-quant + no hints, seq128 b1: fallback_count=8, p95=32.2ms
KV warm-up with write-through (prewrite first 64 tokens): initial spike reduced from +45% -> +12%
```
Alex: that's promising. fewer kernel switches -> lower p95. fallback_count still nonzero; we should improve calibration and quant param selection for layers 10 & 32.
Mira: I'll run per-layer calibration with KL minimization on layers 10 & 32 and re-emit scale/zero for int8 path.
Raj: also add a small compatibility check in the loader: if quant params would cause >2% activation clipping compared to fp16 on calibration set, mark layer as excluded automatically.
Lina: ops runbook item: when we see spike incidents, run `rb-perf-check --model {m} --tag per-layer-quant` to fetch fallback_count and KV warm traces. add this to playbook.
Sam: rollout plan: Canary: 1% traffic -> monitor p95, fallback_count, quality_delta for 1h. If fallback_count>3 or quality_delta>1.5% abort.
Alex: add console alert thresholds: fallback_count_rate > 0.5 per 1000 requests, kv_warm_spike > 25% -> page on-call.
Mira: one more: embeddings & lm_head exclusion worked well on quality; but we should validate for seqgen tasks where top-k sampling is sensitive. add a small decoding-regression test.
Raj: agreed. I'll add evaluation job to the pipeline and attach to PRs that touch quant path.
Cheng: final note: account for older drivers — add device driver check early and fallback to fp16 for known-bad drivers.
Alex: cool. next: @Sam please open a brief RFC with experiment artifacts (configs, perf logs, fallback layer list, per-layer KL plots). aim to ship safe canary next week.
Sam: will do. target PR + RFC by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
Mira: thanks team — really good progress.
CI Bot: created run artifact bundle at https://perf.redwood.local/artifacts/per-layer-quant-probe-1893
Alex: closing the loop — we'll reconvene after RFC.
